title: Chicken and Dumplings
subtitle: American Southern chicken stew with fluffy dropped dumplings
excerpt: The great comfort dish of the American South: a rich chicken stew of shredded chicken thighs and vegetables in a thick, creamy broth, with soft, fluffy dumplings dropped directly into the simmering liquid to cook until light and pillowy. Eaten in deep bowls.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chicken and dumplings is the quintessential comfort food of the American South and the Appalachian region, with roots in the economic necessity of stretching a chicken into a meal for many. The dish exists in two main forms: the Southern style with fluffy, biscuit-like dropped dumplings; and the Pennsylvania Dutch style with thin, flat egg noodle dumplings. The Southern dropped dumpling style is the more widely known. The dumplings are made from a simple baking-powder biscuit dough and are dropped by spoonfuls directly into the simmering broth, where they steam-cook from below in the liquid and from above in the steam trapped under the lid. The result, when done correctly, is a dumpling that is light and fluffy on top, slightly denser at the bottom where it meets the stew, and completely cooked through.

content.text: Do not lift the lid while the dumplings are cooking. The steam trapped inside the pot is what cooks the tops; opening the lid lets it escape and the dumplings remain dense and doughy. The batter should be just mixed: over-mixing makes the dumplings tough. Drop the dumplings in quickly and get the lid on immediately.

Put the chicken thighs in a large pot with the stock, onion, carrot, celery, garlic, thyme, bay leaves, and 1 teaspoon of salt. Bring to the boil, skim, then simmer for 35 minutes until the chicken is cooked through. Remove the chicken and let it cool slightly. Remove the bay leaves. Shred the meat, discarding the skin and bones. Return the meat to the pot.

Melt 40 g of butter in a small pan, add the 3 tablespoons of plain flour, and cook for 1 minute. Whisk in a ladleful of the hot broth until smooth, then pour this back into the pot. Add the cream and stir. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Make the dumplings: mix the 250 g flour, baking powder, 1 teaspoon of salt, and pepper. Add the milk and melted butter and stir until just combined; do not overmix. Drop heaped tablespoons of batter over the surface of the simmering stew, spacing slightly apart. Cover the pot tightly and cook for 15 minutes without lifting the lid. The dumplings are done when a skewer comes out clean. Serve immediately.
